name: portal BFF routes (api/*)
purpose: The Node-runtime server surface: a REST gateway that proxies /api/gateway/* to qip-api with the deployment credential attached and an allowlist for writes, an SSE relay for /api/stream/*, and nine auth routes (sign-up/in/out, verify, reset, csrf, session).
key_contracts: src/app/api/gateway/[...path]/route.ts:74-191 forward() — GET/POST/DELETE proxy, 401 unauthenticated, 405 undeclared write, 500 misconfigured, 502/504 unreachable/timeout
src/app/api/gateway/[...path]/route.ts:98-116 undeclared-write refusal via declaresWrite() before the credential is even read
src/app/api/gateway/[...path]/route.ts:160 redactBody() strips sensitive fields, names them in x-qip-redacted
src/app/api/stream/[channel]/route.ts:33-90 GET — SSE relay, Last-Event-ID forwarded, byte-for-byte passthrough, no buffering
src/app/api/auth/{sign-up,sign-in,sign-out,verify-email,resend-verification,forgot-password,reset-password,session,csrf}/route.ts
production_evidence: These route handlers ARE the portal's server surface; reached whenever the deployed portal.yaml Cloud Run revision serves any /api/* request (see portal app-shell record for deployment evidence). runtime="nodejs", dynamic="force-dynamic" on both gateway and stream routes (route.ts:32-33).
io_and_state: Outbound HTTPS/HTTP to QIP_API_BASE_URL for every call, explicit AbortController timeout (upstream.ts:96, default 10_000ms); reads QIP_API_TOKEN via qip_core-style _FILE indirection (lib/server/secret.ts); mints a Google identity token via the metadata server when QIP_API_AUDIENCE is set (google-credentials.ts). No local persistence in these route files themselves.
status_reason: Write allowlist is structural (checked before the credential is read), redaction is field-declared and legible via a header, and the route table's own comment documents a real incident (a fifth write shipped in the UI/backend and was 405'd here for a whole wave) that the current declaresWrite()-derived tests now guard against.
gaps_observed: src/lib/hooks/useTreasury.ts:196-227 INFLOW_ROUTES (declare/cancel expected inflows) is deliberately NOT added to REST's declaresWrite allowlist — documented as intentional because qip-api itself refuses both routes today for every credential this console holds (no per-person attested principal, ADR 0065/0075/0076); the UI renders the contract text rather than a form.

name: portal lib/server (session, identity, IAP)
purpose: Everything server-only: session cookie sealing/verification, CSRF, the identity service (two providers — a file-backed development store and Google Cloud Identity Platform), IAP assertion verification, and the qip-api credential/token machinery.
key_contracts: session.ts:65 SESSION_TTL_MS (12h), :182/195 sealClaims/unsealClaims, :238/251 hashPassword/verifyPassword (scrypt), :309 csrfAccepted

identity-platform.ts:96,114 gipSignUp/gipSignIn — production provider over Google Identity Toolkit REST, server-side only
iap.ts:292,379 verifyIapAssertion/iapIdentityFrom — ECDSA verification against Google's published keys for ADR 0094's IAP front door

production_evidence: Imported by every /api/auth/* route handler and by /api/gateway and /api/stream for session verification (auth-http.ts sessionForRequest).
io_and_state: node:crypto (scrypt, HMAC, randomBytes); identity-store.ts performs fs I/O (mkdirSync/readFileSync/writeFileSync) but only in the development-provider path — identity-store.ts:13-17 states 'Nothing deployed reaches this file' since the prior /tmp-backed Cloud Run config was replaced by Identity Platform custom claims; outbound HTTPS to identitytoolkit.googleapis.com (identity-platform.ts) and the GCE/Cloud Run metadata server (google-credentials.ts), both with a 10s timeout.
status_reason: Account-enumeration and lockout-tuning are both deliberately withheld from responses (identity.ts doc comment); IAP verification is tested against forged-key, wrong-audience and no-algorithm attacks (iap.spec.ts, 9 tests). identity-store.ts is explicitly documented dead weight in the deployed path now that Identity Platform holds accounts.
gaps_observed: identity-store.ts:13-17 — the development file-backed store is retained in the tree 'so the whole journey works... against no Google project at all' but is explicitly not reached by any deployed process; its prior deployment (Cloud Run /tmp) is documented as a fixed defect (accounts went anonymous on scale-to-zero) rather than a current gap.
